newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Progressive says has no NZ petrol plans.
newsitem.headline: Progressive says has no NZ petrol plans.

text.p: One of New Zealand's biggest supermarket operators Progressive Enterprises said on Friday it was not linked to an expected new entrant into the petrol retailing market in the country.
This week newspapers have reported that a mystery company has bought up to 30 prime sites around the country for stations in a move that might lead to cheaper prices at the pump.

So far the prime suspect, Fletcher Energy, which has in the past expressed an interest in petrol retailing, has declined any comment on the matter, and talk has meanwhile spread that the firm was readying a joint deal with Progressive.
However, Peter Rogers, Progressive's merchandising and marketing manager, told the national NZPA news agency that the company had no plans to combine service stations with supermarkets.
Though he was aware of the international trend for combining food retail with petrol sales he said the company was only keeping an eye on such developments.
A new entrant into the domestic market would compete with the so called "big four," -- Mobil Corp, British Petroleum Co Plc, Shell and Caltex.
About 60 percent of petrol stations in New Zealand are owned by the big four and most of the rest are under contract to them.
FCL Energy recently bought a terminal in Brisbane to store oil and may have done the same in New Zealand, newspapers say.
The company produces about 11 million barrels of oil a year from its New Zealand fields.
